sensors.name: left light sensor LLIGHT (dim inside a tunnel)

control_flow: avoidWalls: if the left light sensor reads less than 70 % (dim light, inside a tunnel), then if the left obstacle sensor sees something it turns left 20°, else if the right obstacle sensor sees something it turns right 20°, else it calls driveInTheDark; if it is bright it calls driveInTheDark.
driveInTheDark: if the left light sensor reads less than 70 % it drives forward at 30 % without end; if it is bright it calls stopAtWall.
stopAtWall: if the front obstacle sensor sees something it stops; otherwise it calls followLine.
followLine: if the line tracker sees black it curves left, otherwise it curves right.

likely_intent.description: Drive in a tunnel without hitting its walls.

decision_points.condition: the left light sensor reads less than 70 % (dim light, inside a tunnel)

branches.outcome: dim light: it checks its left and right obstacle sensors
bright light: it goes on to driveInTheDark

decision_points.condition: first: the left obstacle sensor sees something in front; second: the right obstacle sensor sees something in front

branches.outcome: something in front on its left: it turns left 20°
nothing on its left, something in front on its right: it turns right 20°
nothing on either side: it goes to driveInTheDark, which drives it forward in the dark

scenarios.coded_response: It turns 20° on the spot, to the left when its left sensor sees something in front and to the right when its right sensor sees something, then drives forward at 30 % in the dark.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot starts inside a tunnel, in dim light, and drives along it as it bends.
scenarios.trigger: The tunnel's wall comes in front of the robot's left or right obstacle sensor.
scenarios.title: Doesn't hit the tunnel walls
assumptions: You didn't say what it should do after the bend or whether it should find the tunnel's exit: the tests stop at getting through the bend.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It turns away from the walls and gets through the bend without hitting them.

scenarios.coded_response: It curves left on black and right on the floor, without end.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot starts on a line in bright light.
scenarios.trigger: The line tracker sees black, then the floor, again and again.
scenarios.title: Follows the line in bright light
assumptions: You said nothing about a line: in bright light the program's followLine part does this.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It follows the line to its end.

scenarios.coded_response: It stops, and stops again each round while the wall is in front.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot follows a line in bright light, and a wall stands across the line ahead.
scenarios.trigger: The front obstacle sensor sees the wall.
scenarios.title: Stops at a wall ahead in bright light
assumptions: You said nothing about walls in bright light: the program's stopAtWall part does this.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It stops before the wall without bumping into it.

uncertainties: Your sentence is only about the tunnel walls: in bright light the program also follows a line and stops at a wall ahead, which you didn't mention.
When its left sensor sees a wall the program turns left, towards that side, and when its right sensor sees one it turns right: whether that keeps it off the walls is what the tests show.
In the dark it checks only the left and right obstacle sensors, never the front one.
On a plain floor in bright light it curves right without end, because the line tracker never sees black.
The program loops forever: it has no exit and no goal in it.
